live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the
constructor's summary

value.label: Independent assessment

value.definition: Author identity identifies the party responsible for a realised subject's content. Actor identity identifies whoever performs an operation and is not itself authority. Independence depends on authorship and evidence conditions.

grounding.quote:
Author identity is the party responsible for the content of a realised
subject. It is distinct from actor identity, whoever performs one
operation, which is an identity and not an authority

value.label: Author identity and actor identity

value.definition: A review returns one core result per declared predicate actually evaluated, together with exact subject and basis, consulted evidence, consequence-ranked findings, evidence and smallest bounded correction for each finding, residual uncertainty and invalidation conditions.
exceptions: A planned predicate not evaluated has no result.

grounding.quote:
A review returns one core result
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
invalidation conditions.

value.label: Review result

conditions: A review returns findings with technical triage.
value.definition: Technical triage is the assessor's evidence-bound assessment against the exact evaluated claim and basis. Severity grades consequence as evaluation evidence. Priority, current promotion-boundary effect and disposition belong to the decision owner. Triage payload classes complete, indeterminate and not_applicable are distinct from core results, dispositions, priorities and lifecycle states.

grounding.quote:
Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's

value.label: Technical triage

conditions: The predicate has actually been evaluated.
value.definition: The review projection distinguishes satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis. Missing evaluation is absence of a result, not an additional value or an indeterminate value.

grounding.quote:
A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
`indeterminate` never stands for it.
| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

value.label: Core review-result domain

value.definition: Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged evaluated subject, bounded to its named instance and interval. Work-item closure is satisfaction of that item's stated closing condition.
value.label: Acceptance and work-item closure

conditions: The accepted subject is a successor.
value.definition: Acceptance evidence identifying the exact predecessor immutable cut and one semantic disposition for every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor; RELEASE §9 owns its disposition values and evaluation.

grounding.quote:
Where the subject is a successor, its acceptance evidence includes the
successor disposition record of [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(STDO-UP-015), which states the law: the exact predecessor immutable cut
the successor evolves, and one semantic disposition for every predecessor
claim capable of affecting the successor.

value.label: Successor disposition record

value.definition: A finding is a defect reported against the exact evaluated claim. Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act over a finding. EVALUATION §5 owns the common blocking rule; profiles and work carriers add only domain triggers.

grounding.quote:
A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it
evaluated (§4). Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act
over that finding (§4, Result and triage projection). This section is the
one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
refer to it and add only their domain triggers.

value.label: Finding and promotion block

value.definition: A realisation conforms to specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract and independent judgment. Semantic conformance uses the governing semantic basis as Σ.

grounding.quote:
A realisation aⱼ conforms to a specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour
satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract (P1) and an independent
judgment (P6).

value.label: Conformance of realisations

value.definition: The equivalence ladder lists, without ordering or implication, conformance, semantic equivalence, computational equivalence and categorical equivalence. Semantic equivalence here concerns identical interpreted behaviour of two realisations, or a realisation and declared reference outcome, on a stated domain including behaviour outside Σ; it is not bounded-context concept equivalence. Computational equivalence concerns the same function at equal cost for declared workloads on architecture H. Categorical equivalence concerns categories and maps; preservation of identities and composition is a further distinct claim.

grounding.quote:
the rungs are listed, not ordered, and no rung implies
another. Conformance, semantic equivalence, computational equivalence and
categorical equivalence are separate claims with separate evidence

Computational
equivalence claims that two realisations compute the same function at
equal cost for declared workloads on a declared architecture H.

value.label: Equivalence ladder

conditions: A specification is arranged in layers.
value.definition: Layered sufficiency means a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer. Derivation need not be unique. Reconstructability requires a correct route, with scope determined by the claim.

grounding.quote:
A specification arranged in layers is sufficient when
a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer; the
derivation need not be unique

value.label: Layered sufficiency and reconstructability

conditions: A task builds or assesses one successor member against its predecessor.
value.definition: A reconstruction return separates three claims and their evidence: semantic conservation reads both texts against a predecessor claim's disposition; demonstrated reduction traces a cheaper corresponding deciding path on a declared measure with tradeoffs; mere relocation moves text between owners or carriers without changed meaning or a traced deciding-path change.

grounding.quote:
Demonstrated
reduction: a deciding path of the successor costs less than the same path
in the predecessor on a declared measure, shown by the trace of both paths
with the declared tradeoffs. Mere relocation: text moved from one owner or
carrier to another without a change in meaning and without a traced
change in any deciding path.

value.label: Return of a reconstruction

conditions: One specification may have several realisations.
Fallible constructors produce realisations, frames and methods relied on by other actors.
Qualification evidence comprises finite cases run within declared actor envelopes.
value.definition: F7, conformance, equivalence and qualification, covers EVALUATION §§6–7 and CONFORMANCE. Its instance premises are conditions of governed work, not commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. It explicitly invokes P0's actor-change premise: a later actor may reacquire declared sources but not private memory. Its table traces consequences and added policy choices without deciding them.

grounding.quote:
P0's actor-change premise, that the actor of one
step need not be the actor of the next and may re-acquire declared sources
but not private memory, is cited by name.

value.label: Conformance, equivalence and qualification

value.definition: Document section grouping frame qualification and qualification of the method; the heading alone adds no qualification procedure.

grounding.quote: ## 7. Qualification of frames and of the method

value.label: Qualification of frames and of the method

value.definition: Qualification of a candidate frame is proportional to its claims and binds the exact evaluated frame revision, actor envelope, evaluation family, basis class and evidence conditions.

grounding.quote:
Qualification binds the exact frame revision, actor envelope, evaluation
family, basis class and evidence conditions evaluated. It does not
generalise to an unevaluated population by naming the frame generically

value.label: Frame qualification

value.definition: Fit asks whether an actor class can hold a frame; context fit compares measured selected-representation size with declared capacity. grounding.quote:
Whether the actor class
operates the frame adequately is adequate attention, and only actual-use
evidence establishes it

value.label: Fit and adequate attention

value.definition: Qualification of generic method sufficiency uses the ordinary work boundary, construction and assessment relation, and layered sufficiency, with no second process. Constructor, freeze, assessor, acceptance and release protocols are supplied by governing authority rather than defined by this member.

grounding.quote:
The method is qualified the way it qualifies anything else. Qualification
of generic method sufficiency consumes the work boundary (FOUNDATIONS §2),
the construction and assessment relation of ACTIVATION §1 and the layered
sufficiency of §6; it creates no second process.

value.label: Method self-qualification

value.definition: The qualification population includes every claimed function and failure relation: declare, activate, evaluate, conjoin, translate, audit_coverage, revise, result consumption and material composition. grounding.quote:
The qualification population is every function and failure relation the
method claims (REFERENCE_FRAME §5), each with its required representative
observations (P6):

value.label: Method-function qualification population

conditions: Guidance derived from the method changes.

Changed derived guidance, a compression, a frame packet,
a skill or any other projection of the method, is qualified against
source-derived expected behaviour, including the affected permissions,
exclusions and invalidators.

For a selected activation, measure whether a fresh actor given
only the published documents recovers the governing relations with fidelity
judged independently, and at what reconstruction cost, against the rc.2
corpus as baseline.

Also new: the tables of families F6 (§1) and F7 (§6), in
the format of FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law; each decides nothing and

conditions: The Product separately adopts the optional profile.

grounding.quote:
An operational
profile owns only its own bindings, the terms and choices it adds for its

conditions: The executive configuration is selected.
value.definition: Worker carries constructor responsibility; Reviewer carries assessor responsibility; Executive coordinates and disposes as decision owner or admitted bounded proxy under an existing grant. These overlapping evaluation contexts are neither a hierarchy nor actor topology, and names confer no authority.

grounding.quote:
the Worker frame carries the constructor's, the Reviewer
frame the assessor's, and the Executive frame is the configuration's
coordinator, which disposes as decision owner or its admitted proxy within
the grant existing authority admits.

The three frames are overlapping evaluation contexts. They are neither a
hierarchy nor an actor topology

value.label: Executive, Worker and Reviewer frames

value.definition: Twelve available specialist-frame families: Product, Product Composition, Design, Design Component, Public Boundary, Entity, Operator, Owner, Effect, Reuse/Foundation, Install and Proof. They separate recurring questions concerning constitutional WHAT, structural HOW, identity, authority, effects, foundations, installed subjects and evidence; they are not mandatory actors, stages, components, services, files or runtime types.

grounding.quote:
The profile derives twelve generic specialist-frame families (§11):
Product, Product Composition, Design, Design Component, Public Boundary,
Entity, Operator, Owner, Effect, Reuse/Foundation, Install and Proof.

value.label: Generic specialist-frame families

value.definition: User acceptance, end to end, integration and unit are ASSURANCE-owned tier-2 testing frames. Their evidence topology assigns claims to congruent evidence frames; using them in this profile adds no role, stage, authority or testing hierarchy.

grounding.quote:
The four product testing frames (user acceptance, end to end, integration,
unit) are tier-2 law in ASSURANCE §7. Under this profile they are activated
inside the same conditionally selected engagement relation; they add no
role, stage, authority or testing hierarchy.

value.label: Product testing frames

value.definition: The concrete Project Reference-Frame Basis belongs to the adopting Product's authority; PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7 owns the Product-binding relation, REFERENCE_FRAME owns pure frame principles, and the optional profile owns its mappings.

grounding.quote:
Three ownership layers stay distinct:
REFERENCE_FRAME owns the pure frame principles; this member owns the
optional Executive, Worker, Reviewer and specialist mappings; PRODUCT_DEFINITION
§7 owns the Product-binding relation, and each adopting Product's authority
owns its concrete Project Reference-Frame Basis.

value.label: Project Reference-Frame Basis

value.definition: Direct entry and coordinated engagement are conditionally selected routes under ACTIVATION. Within the executive configuration Worker, also called Writer, is the directly entering frame and Executive the coordinating frame.

grounding.quote:
Where the
executive configuration is selected, the directly entering frame is Worker
(Writer) and the coordinating frame Executive. A role or frame name alone
creates no review obligation either

value.label: Direct and coordinated engagement

value.definition: F16, Engagement baseline, is an operational profile. Its foundation-to-law trace distinguishes imported consequences, foundational commitments, profile choices and adopting-Product choices. Inclusion in a method cut makes it available; adoption is a separate Product-authority act.

grounding.quote:
This member is material family F16, Engagement baseline (operational
profile).

value.label: Engagement baseline

value.definition: An engagement frame evaluates selection, construction, assessment or disposition of governed work. Executive, Worker and Reviewer are the profile's engagement frames.

grounding.quote:
An engagement frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation family
concerns selecting, constructing, assessing or disposing governed work.
Executive, Worker and Reviewer are this profile's engagement frames (P1;
rc.2 #engagement-frame).

value.label: Engagement frame

value.definition: An activated Product, requirement, design, identity, release, domain, implementation, test, operational, historical or capability frame needed by one engagement evaluation.

grounding.quote:
A specialist frame is an activated Product, requirement, design, identity,
release, domain, implementation, test, operational, historical or
capability frame that one engagement evaluation needs.

value.label: Specialist frame

value.definition: A reusable evaluation-family archetype naming a recurring distinction. It selects no concrete carrier, component, actor, architecture, owner or implementation.

grounding.quote:
A generic specialist-frame family is a reusable evaluation-family archetype
of this profile (§11). It names a recurring distinction that a project
either instantiates where material, has capable authority establish as
non-material for the governed outcome, or keeps as an explicit coverage
residual (P2, P6; rc.2 #generic-specialist-frame-family).

value.label: Generic specialist-frame family

value.definition: Testing frame, authoritative Product path and material combinatorial complexity are tier-2 terms owned by ASSURANCE §7 and used here without additions.

grounding.quote:
Testing frame, authoritative Product path and material combinatorial
complexity are tier-2 terms defined in ASSURANCE §7. This profile uses them
as defined there and adds nothing to them (P1; rc.2 #testing-frame,
#authoritative-product-path, #material-combinatorial-complexity).

value.label: ASSURANCE-owned terms

value.definition: The frame selecting or confirming bounded activation configuration and consuming closed Worker and Reviewer results under existing project decision authority. Its complete Product view and current MVP or release mandate support priority, disposition and selection of the next authorised action; this view is not the complete workspace.

grounding.quote:
Executive is this profile's label for the frame that selects or confirms
the bounded activation configuration and consumes closed Worker and
Reviewer results under existing project decision authority. It holds the
complete Product view and the current MVP or release mandate needed to
assign priority, apply disposition and select the next authorised action
(P6, P2; rc.2 #executive).

value.label: Executive

value.definition: The ACTIVATION constructor role activated as a frame, owning construction and self-review within exact intake through operation authority inherited from the governing work relation. Writer is its document-and-record specialisation.

grounding.quote:
Worker is this profile's label for the constructor role of ACTIVATION §1
activated as a frame. It owns construction and self-review inside its exact
intake, through the operation authority inherited from the governing work
relation. It acquires no admission, publication, acceptance or continuation
authority (P6; rc.2 #worker).

value.label: Worker

value.definition: An activated independent live-surface evaluation consumed by the assessment relation. It evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result, adding evidence-bound technical triage when a finding exists.

grounding.quote:
Reviewer is this profile's label for the independent live-surface
evaluation that the assessment relation of ACTIVATION §1 consumes, governed
by EVALUATION §3 (independence and traceability) and EVALUATION §1 and §7
(assurance boundary and qualification freeze), activated as a frame. It
evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result, with evidence-bound
technical triage when a finding exists.

value.label: Reviewer

value.definition: Reviewer assessment of one finding against its exact evaluated claim and basis. Its supportable payload comprises affected claim and observed failure, Product-scaled severity, causal assessment and quantified-assurance confidence, blast radius and affected users/paths/relations, workaround or containment, repair complexity, regression risk, material dependencies, residual uncertainty and evidence that would reduce it.
value.label: Technical triage

value.definition: Four distinct values are severity, priority, frame result and current-boundary effect. Severity grades a finding's consequence if manifested and is Reviewer evidence. Priority is an Executive decision ordering response relative to complete Product outcome, likelihood/exposure, MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, delay cost and capacity. Current-boundary effect records blocks, requires narrowing, or may remain an explicit residual; it is a decision projection with no independent core value or disposition.

grounding.quote:
Severity grades the consequence if the finding manifests. Priority orders
the response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and
exposure, the current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies,
cost of delay and available capacity. The Reviewer grades severity; the
Executive assigns priority (P6, P2).

Current-boundary effect is the Executive's recorded determination of what
one finding does to the current promotion boundary: it blocks it, requires
narrowing it, or may remain an explicit residual. It is a decision
projection, a state this profile declares, not a result and not a
disposition (§8): it maps to no core value of its own and decides nothing
by itself.

value.label: Severity, priority, frame result and current-boundary effect

conditions: A Worker has been lawfully and successfully activated.
value.definition: The Worker's closed output to its declared consumer, which is the Executive in the coordinated branch. Construction availability has five total, exclusive values mapped to one core value each: candidate_ready→satisfied; refused→falsified; incomplete→falsified; re_entry_requested(authority)→out_of_frame; re_entry_requested(basis)→invalid_basis. These are carriers, neither assessment nor acceptance nor new dispositions.

grounding.quote:
The work-result values are the five values of construction availability,
the refinement that
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability) defines for the
predicate "a candidate is available". ACTIVATION §3 owns their grounds,
maps each to exactly one core value, and states that the mapping is total
and exclusive after lawful activation. In this profile they are carriers,
not new semantic dispositions, and none of them is an assessment or an
acceptance of the candidate (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results).

value.label: Work result

value.definition: Subject identity required by transition evidence and traceability. It is frozen before material reference exposure where generic method qualification requires; elsewhere immutable identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation stabilises it sufficiently for the claimed assessment. This introduces no lifecycle state named frozen.

grounding.quote:
An exact candidate is the subject identity that the transition evidence of
ACTIVATION §7 and the traceability of EVALUATION §3 require. Where generic
method qualification applies (EVALUATION §7), its construction result is
frozen before material reference exposure as that clause requires.
Elsewhere this profile stabilises the review subject through an immutable
identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation sufficient for the claimed
assessment. The profile creates no new lifecycle state named `frozen` (P3,
P6; rc.2 #exact-candidate).

value.label: Exact candidate

conditions: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis adopts the profile.
value.definition: Projection inside the Product-owned basis recording selected profile mapping, exact outcome, actor envelopes, evidence coordinates and revision conditions additional to Product binding. It consumes that basis, creates no second basis and mints no projected authority.

grounding.quote:
A baseline-adoption projection consumes the Product-owned Project
Reference-Frame Basis of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7. Where that basis adopts
this profile, the projection records the selected profile mapping, exact
outcome, actor envelopes, evidence coordinates and revision conditions
needed in addition to the Product binding (§16). It is not a second
frame-basis definition and mints none of the authority it projects (P6;
rc.2 #baseline-adoption-projection).

value.label: Baseline-adoption projection

value.definition: The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis projects existing owners' decisions and cites every material configuration source without becoming a new local-axiom authority.

grounding.quote:
The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7)
cites every material source of the configuration and does not collapse
them into a new local-axiom authority (P6).

value.label: Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis

value.definition: A finite decision-driven cycle maintaining the unresolved material-evaluation frontier and closed-result ledger, activating dependency-ready evaluations on exact outcome and basis and updating coverage, dependencies, conflicts and discovered materiality.

grounding.quote:
U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis

while U is non-empty:
  select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
  activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
  keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results
  when no other authorised decision is ready:
    await decision-relevant input (event-driven attention, below)
  record every closed result, technical triage, residual and invalidation condition
  apply only declared conjunctions or translations
  assign priority and boundary effect only under the current Product mandate
  invalidate affected results when the subject or basis changes
  update U from coverage, dependencies, conflicts and discovered materiality

value.label: Attention cycle

value.definition: Five pre-activation and pre-disposition checks: outcome lock covers unchanged Goal, Product outcome, boundary, lawful re-entry class, mandate and triage policy; basis lock covers exact/current subject, authority, dependency, configuration, topology, evidence, time and candidate; Product-role lock keeps lineage identities distinct and Development Product bound to exact Install; authority lock covers unchanged semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance and publication owners/grants; coverage-and-return lock requires every material evaluation/interaction closed or explicit residual and every consumed result on its declared return relation.

grounding.quote:
| outcome lock | the selected Goal, Product outcome, boundary and lawful re-entry class, the current MVP or release mandate, and the triage policy are unchanged |
| basis lock | the subject, authority, dependency, configuration, topology, evidence, time and candidate coordinates are exact and current |
| Product-role lock | the mutable Source Project, Product Definition, Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact and dependent Product identities stay distinct, and every Development Product role stays bound to its exact underlying Install |
| authority lock | the semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance and publication owners and grants are unchanged |
| coverage-and-return lock | every material evaluation and interaction is closed or an explicit residual, and every consumed result followed its declared return relation |

value.label: Drift locks

value.definition: A governed outcome's basis for one Product or an explicit directed Product chain. It records distinct mutable Source Project, current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product and composition-edge roles. Every Development Product binds one exact Install; each edge names source/target roles, governing authority/contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and invalidation.

grounding.quote:
A governed outcome may concern one Product or an explicit directed chain of
Products. Its basis records the distinct role of every mutable Source
Project, current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release
Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product and
composition edge. Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying
Install identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, its governing
authority and contracts, its lifecycle, its evidence boundary, its refusal
and its invalidation (P3, P6; rc.2 #product-chain-basis; the Product-role
map in the basis is PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7, the lineage objects FOUNDATIONS
§2).

value.label: Product-chain basis

conditions: Bounded change and delivery management across successive tasks need separate attention.
value.definition: One lawful task-fit configuration allocating construction to Worker/Writer, required assessment to Reviewer and cross-task coordination/disposition within an admitted decision grant to Executive. It is not the method default or a role inventory required for all work.
exceptions: Where one sufficient frame covers the task, direct entry applies instead.

grounding.quote:
It allocates construction to the Worker frame, specialised as Writer for
documents and records; assessment, where it is required, to the Reviewer
frame; and coordination across tasks to the Executive frame, which disposes
within the decision grant existing authority admits (§5, §8 to §10). It is
one configuration, selected where it fits the task, not an inventory of
roles that all work needs.

value.label: Executive configuration

value.definition: The smallest real runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through the selected composition. This profile's delivery strategy establishes it early, widens it in bounded increments, or extends/revalidates an existing affected thread. Its objective is early composition feedback at the cost of later widening.

grounding.quote:
The Executive sequences delivery around a steel thread: the smallest real,
runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through
the selected composition. The path is established early and widened in
bounded increments; where it already exists, the affected thread is extended
or revalidated. Increments are chosen for consequential uncertainty,
dependency and interface reach, and failure impact (P2; rc.2
#steel-thread-delivery; the generic sequencing heuristic is SPEC_METHOD §8).

value.label: Steel thread

value.definition: Evaluation archetype asking whether one exact current Product claim, outcome, boundary and lifecycle governs its subject without downstream reinterpretation; basis includes current Intent, Product, requirements, acceptance meaning and exact coordinates.

grounding.quote: Does one exact current Product claim, outcome, boundary and lifecycle govern the claimed Product subject without downstream reinterpretation?

value.label: Product evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype for one exact directed Product relation preserving source/target roles, Product Definition, Release Cut, Product and Install identities, Development Product role binding, contracts, authority, lifecycle, evidence boundary and invalidation law. Chains use bounded edge activations and declared conjunction.

grounding.quote: A chain is evaluated through bounded edge activations and a declared conjunction.

value.label: Product Composition evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype asking whether accepted structural HOW satisfies material constitutional WHAT, closes required design relations and preserves owners across affected topology.

grounding.quote: Does the accepted structural HOW satisfy the material constitutional WHAT, close the required design relations and keep their owners across the affected topology?

value.label: Design evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype for a bounded design component and its direct causal dependency cone, checking preservation of parent contract, internal relations, sibling seams and required outputs.

grounding.quote: Does one bounded design component, with its direct causal dependency cone, preserve its parent contract, internal relations, sibling seams and required outputs?

value.label: Design Component evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking that a supported public entry/exit performs exactly assigned validation, selection, transport, refusal and projection while preserving selected interior owners.

grounding.quote: Does one supported public entry or exit perform exactly its assigned validation, selection, transport, refusal and projection relations while preserving the selected interior owners?

value.label: Public Boundary evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking one semantic, artifact or runtime entity's exact identity, kind, lifecycle, owner, representation and applicable effect regime.

grounding.quote: Is one semantic, artifact or runtime entity bound to its exact identity, kind, lifecycle, owner, representation and applicable effect regime?

value.label: Entity evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype for a material operation as an irreducible declared relation over admitted domain, inputs, outputs, refusals, algebra, effects and lawful compositions.

grounding.quote: Is one material operation an irreducible declared relation over its admitted domain, inputs, outputs, refusals, algebra, effects and lawful compositions?

value.label: Operator evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking preservation of owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle, refusal invariants and permitted delegation for one semantic or authority-bearing relation.

grounding.quote: Does one semantic or authority-bearing relation preserve its owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle, refusal invariants and permitted delegation?

value.label: Owner evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking an action's declared pure, observational, artifact or runtime effect regime, including material commit, failure, retry, recovery, compensation, admission and projection law.

grounding.quote: Does one action obey its declared pure, observational, artifact or runtime effect regime, including commit, failure, retry, recovery, compensation, admission and projection law where material?

value.label: Effect evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking normalisation and bounded comparison of a material generic capability/dependency against credible lawful foundations, preserving irreducible local remainder and authority-bearing role.

grounding.quote: Has one material generic capability or dependency been normalised and compared against credible lawful foundations, with any irreducible local remainder and authority-bearing role preserved?

value.label: Reuse/Foundation evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking exact selected Product, release, artifact, dependency set, configuration and callable entry resolved and exercised through admitted installed coordinates independently of mutable-source convenience.

grounding.quote: Is the exact selected Product, release, artifact, dependency set, configuration and callable entry resolved and exercised through its admitted installed coordinate, independently of mutable source convenience?

value.label: Install evaluation family

value.definition: Evaluation archetype checking congruent subject, basis, path, population, oracle, evidence, falsifier, residual boundary and invalidation law for one exact claim.

grounding.quote: Does one exact claim have a congruent subject, basis, path, population, oracle, evidence, falsifier, residual boundary and invalidation law?

value.label: Proof evaluation family

value.definition: ASSURANCE-owned user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration and unit testing frames retain distinct claims and coordinates. The end-to-end interface integration frame relates specialist families to integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance; computational whole-path evaluation composes selected interface claims with Operator, Owner, Reuse/Foundation and Proof.

grounding.quote:
The end-to-end interface integration frame (ASSURANCE §13) relates the
Public Boundary, Design, Operator, Owner and Proof families to the
integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance frames. Its computational
whole-path evaluation composes the selected interface claims with Operator,
Owner, Reuse/Foundation and Proof. Neither adds a thirteenth family, a fifth
testing type, a role or a universal activation gate (P2; rc.2
#derived-end-to-end-interface-integration-frame,
#computational-whole-path-evaluation).

value.label: Testing and interface frames

value.definition: Eight bounded transfer projections: Worker activation, activation refusal, work result, Reviewer activation, review result, specialist activation, specialist result, and disposition/checkpoint. They carry exact declared relations and coordinates through admitted existing carriers.

grounding.quote:
The coordinated branch uses the following bounded projections. They may be
fields in existing Goals, tickets, design assets, commentary, qualification
or release evidence, or other admitted carriers; the profile requires no new
artifact type (P2, P6; rc.2 #handoff-projection).

value.label: Handoff projection

value.definition: Known material-evaluation inventory derived from selected method members, domain, outcome, history, dependencies and workspace. Coverage is the union of admissible observations contributed by activated frames, retaining unknown, uncovered, conditional, conflicted and authority-excluded residuals.

grounding.quote:
The Executive derives the complete known evaluation inventory from the
selected method members, the project domain, the outcome, history,
dependencies and the workspace. Operational full coverage keeps every
unknown, uncovered, conditional, conflicted or authority-excluded residual
REFERENCE_FRAME §8 requires (P4b, P5).

value.label: Evaluation inventory and coverage

value.definition: A configuration defined by Product, requirement, Goals or accepted-design authority that may use different frames, names, overlap, sequences and actor bindings while retaining applicable method relations and explicit claim coverage.

grounding.quote:
A project may define different frames, names, overlaps, sequences and actor
bindings. The defining Product, requirement, Goals or accepted-design
authority records (P6, P2; rc.2 #define-a-project-configuration;
REFERENCE_FRAME §4):

value.label: Project-defined configuration

value.definition: The Executive baseline distinguishes frames from actors. Activation binds an actor to a frame. Executive, Worker and Reviewer are finite evaluation frames available for applicable engagements, not actor identities or an organisational hierarchy.

grounding.quote:
Frames and actors are separate identities: activation binds an actor to
a frame

Executive, Worker and Reviewer are available finite evaluation frames,
   activated only where applicable, not a hierarchy or actor identities;

value.label: Executive baseline frames

value.definition: Profile qualification applies frame qualification and method self-qualification under EVALUATION §7, creating no separate protocol. A profile trial evaluates this profile and its declared composition with the exact REFERENCE_FRAME basis; neither becomes a peer authority.

grounding.quote:
Qualification of this profile applies frame qualification and method
self-qualification (EVALUATION §7); it creates no other qualification
protocol

value.label: Profile qualification and representative trial

conditions: A Product adopts the optional Executive baseline.
value.definition: The Executive Baseline Adoption Additions template supplements the §16 adoption record and the Project Reference-Frame Basis and starter template owned by PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7. It requests: exact profile identity; Executive, Worker and Reviewer declaration or acquisition references; role-specific capability, authority and independence bindings; Product severity and priority scales, current-boundary cutoff, non-waivable hard stops and Reviewer-to-Executive triage relation; referenced ACTIVATION §3 construction-availability mapping, with project refinements mapped to their parent value's core value; declarations, non-material evidence or residuals for all twelve generic families; Product-testing claims, frame topology, material combination populations, scenario matrix, oracles and required/forbidden authoritative paths; profile-specific activation-refusal, closed-result, conjunction and return relations; and qualification evidence and residuals.

grounding.quote: # Executive Baseline Adoption Additions

value.label: Executive Baseline Adoption Additions template

value.definition: The adoption record owned by §16 Adopt this baseline incorporates both its own list and the profile-specific additions as one record. Its statement decides any item appearing in both lists.

grounding.quote:
an adopting Product
records both lists as one record, and where an item appears in both, the
§16 statement decides it

value.label: Baseline adoption record

value.definition: Frame-specific additions extend the generic minimal activation binding: Worker execution intake and applicable mutation grant details; Reviewer claim, assessment, independence and technical-triage details; Executive Product, mandate, evaluation, policy, result and disposition details.

grounding.quote:
Every activation first carries the generic binding of REFERENCE_FRAME §11
(minimal activation binding).

value.label: Baseline activation additions

value.definition: An observation-to-first-diagnosis table routes evaluation without predetermining a verdict.

grounding.quote: The table routes evaluation; it does not predetermine a verdict

value.label: Failure classification

value.definition: Thirty-two identified ways of misapplying the optional profile, covering frame identity, grants, result routing, review independence, evidence, testing, generic families and triage.

grounding.quote: The profile is misapplied when

value.label: Profile anti-patterns

conditions: An exact outcome and engagement branch have been selected.
value.definition: Baseline application to one outcome evaluates only applicable obligations. Work-item closure applies the existing TICKETS §7 condition, not Reviewer approval or the occurrence of a review. A closed indeterminate result does not satisfy an unresolved obligation.

grounding.quote:
Only the obligations applicable to the exact selected outcome and
engagement branch are evaluated.

value.label: Branch-relative baseline closure

value.definition: The source-disposition table records routes from rc.2 STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md anchors to successor loci. Conserved rows are said to be restated in tenant text; routes are provenance only, including duplicate listings in ASSURANCE and EVALUATION. Heading-only predecessor rows are marked not applicable. Several synthetic child rows and the first failure-classification row describe proposed supersessions pending the Product owner's acceptance.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is restated in tenant text at its locus; a route is
provenance only.

value.label: Baseline predecessor-disposition ledger

value.definition: The subject's Tier 1 FOUNDATIONS member owns the vocabulary of standing; ontology of frames, authority, lineage and work boundaries; construction accounts and imports; P0–P6 commitments, consequence-trace format and family index; composition, conservation, core results, conjunction and categorical-demonstration requirements; and hypotheses. Other members import or refine these definitions without redefining their owner.

grounding.quote: Tier 1. Owns the vocabulary of standing (§1);

value.label: FOUNDATIONS member

value.definition: A foundational claim is a commitment or hypothesis and has exactly one standing: recovered, an adopted premise consolidating named source rules without treating them as proof; independent, an adopted premise argued by a case where other commitments hold and it fails; derived, a consequence with its premises named; or hypothesis, established by no method clause or argument, not law and retained for falsification. This differs from what a result establishes about its predicate and from a successor's disposition of a predecessor claim.

grounding.quote: Each has exactly one of four standings:

value.label: Foundational standing

value.definition: Four distinct meanings of join: categorical join is a map between categories; composition boundary joins successive steps; result join combines closed results under one decision rule; relation join is an equality join of participants in an enclosing relation. Unqualified join in a result context means result join.

grounding.quote: Four uses of "join" in this corpus are distinct

value.label: Distinct join meanings

value.definition: Subject is the exact thing a claim, representation or transformation concerns, specified by inventory and bytes or semantic addresses. Representation is bytes, text, model or program standing for it; equal representations do not establish equal meaning. Interpretation is a declared representation-to-meaning contract stating reliable distinctions and residuals within a Context, whose declared scope includes subject, definitions, basis and admissible observations.

grounding.quote: | Interpretation | a declared contract from representation to meaning within a context; says which distinctions a consumer may rely on and which are residual | P1 |

value.label: Subject, representation, interpretation and context

value.definition: Outcome U is a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval against which transformation adequacy is judged. Object O is a subject with scoped identity (authority, kind, value), boundary, current state and declared material relations; identity survives admissible state and encoding change.

grounding.quote: | Outcome U | a selected, owner-defined, directly verifiable state with an acceptance interval; adequacy of a transformation is judged against it | P2 |

value.label: Outcome U and Object O

value.definition: Actor performs a step within a capability envelope of context, attention, time and capability; roles are occupied relations selected by configuration, not actor kinds. Step is a bounded unit comprising intake, selected context, grant, execution and output. A step-produced fact is a judgment, residual, observation or authority decision produced by a step that cannot be reacquired from declared sources; reproducible observations are excluded.

grounding.quote: | Step | one bounded unit of work: intake, selected context, grant, execution, output | P0 |

value.label: Actor, step and step-produced fact

value.definition: Claim is an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier. Evidence is exact admitted observations or artifacts carrying provenance, subject identity, basis and scope; availability in a frame confers neither semantic truth nor decision authority. Judgment is a recorded evaluation over an unchanged subject with evaluator, decision, evidence, scope and revising observation. Residual is material uncertainty, omission, loss or unproven relation remaining until authorised disposition.

grounding.quote: | Claim | an assertion with subject, property, basis, witness relation and falsifier | P6 |

value.label: Claim, evidence, judgment and residual

value.definition: Basis is the exact state binding a step, claim, result or evaluation, including every material version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration and evidence coordinate. It is immutable or moving with declared advancement detection and reevaluation conditions; mixed bases require an explicit composite relation. Materiality is evaluation-relative: lawful change can change a result, invalidate its basis, change admissible evidence, change who may perform a material operation, or change who may decide an evaluation or material operation; uncertainty and closure are material on the same grounds.

grounding.quote: materiality is evaluation-relative, so a relation material in one frame may be irrelevant in another

value.label: Basis and materiality

value.definition: Evaluation is a declared question with known admissible result family, evidence basis, decision authority and operation authority where material action occurs; it may seek judgment, prediction, construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification or action recommendation. An evaluation family needs the same material-relation manifold, authority basis and result algebra; similar wording is insufficient.

grounding.quote: similar wording does not prove that two evaluations share a family

value.label: Evaluation and evaluation family

value.definition: Workspace is the bounded material reasoned over or acted on, potentially including constitutional sources, assets, designs, implementations, tools, runtime, evidence, history, dependencies and human decisions; a repository is only one possible carrier. Material-relation manifold is the finite jointly interpretable variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities, observations and exclusions an evaluation family needs; charts may overlap and imply neither geometric mathematics nor runtime abstraction. Coordinate is the complete locally required basis, identity, lineage, input, evidence and authority position. Topology is the visible relation structure of entities, capabilities, authorities, lifecycle state spaces, adjacencies and seams at one basis, not necessarily the whole workspace.

grounding.quote: no geometric mathematics or runtime abstraction is implied

value.label: Workspace, manifold, coordinate and topology

value.definition: Capability envelope specifies competence, context capacity, tools, access, applicable evaluation or assurance independence, and configuration required for activation and evaluation. Reference frame is a finite specification of attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations for one declared evaluation family over a stated basis. Activated frame binds a declaration to exact evaluation, workspace subject, basis, actor and evidence-acquisition boundary; declaration reuse is not proof of activation correctness.

grounding.quote: a reusable declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct

value.label: Reference frame, activation and capability envelope

value.definition: Frame set is the human-declared available family for an outcome or workspace, potentially with overlaps, alternatives, specialist, exploratory and separately activated assurance frames; it need not be a partition, tree, stack or exhaustive ontology. Active configuration consists of frame activations and declared result relations for one evaluation or decision, whether one frame or multiple disjoint, overlapping or composed frames. Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it

to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:

conditions: An evaluation was required or planned but not performed.
value.definition: Absence of a closed result, distinct from every core value, including indeterminate. A missing result enters conjunction as a planned assessment without an applicable closed result when planned, or as uncovered required coverage when no assessment addresses the obligation.

grounding.quote:
Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it

indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.

value.definition: Three separate result predicates: availability asks whether a step produced a candidate; assessment asks whether the candidate meets declared criteria; acceptance asks whether the decision owner accepts it at its boundary. A step's stop state answers a further, separate question.

Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
its declared criteria; and that the
[decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step (P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),

The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
  questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's

value.definition: Combination of results into one result for a composite predicate: component claims, a decision over evaluations, or the outer contract of composed steps. Its three distinct inputs are returned closed results with predicates and domain outcomes; planned assessments lacking an applicable closed result; and required coverage R minus coverage C admitted by planned assessments.

grounding.quote:
Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a

the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6).

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the

   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

The cited ACTIVATION, EVALUATION, ASSURANCE, RELEASE, SPEC_METHOD and a_c surfaces apply these relations without stating a second relation. The relations below connect construction to the assertions, observations
and evidence that support claims about it. They are the shared owner for
the preservation, assertion, provenance, quantified-assurance, reuse and
formal-representation obligations in this corpus; ACTIVATION §1, §4, §5 and §7, EVALUATION §1 and §3,
ASSURANCE §3, §10, §11 and §14, RELEASE §8 and §9, SPEC_METHOD §4 and
the a_c interpretation apply them and state no second relation (P6). They are law
carried from the common assurance requirement. A tenant chooses its
representation and execution within these obligations. The notation
states proof obligations; writing an implication does not discharge it.

Foundation to law. This family, assurance relations, covers the six
subsections that follow. Its instance premises are: (a) a construction
with the governing basis bound at intake under ACTIVATION §1 and the
material assumptions, together written Γ here; (b) a declared domain Ω of cases, each with the inputs,
behaviour and environment material to an obligation; (c) a checker with

Claimed preservation is the universal obligation: for all x,x', P_i(x) and F_i(x,x') implies P_(i+1)(x').

For a sequence of transformations, let `X_i` be the state or trace domain
at boundary i, `F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1)` the declared transition relation, and
`P_i` the property to retain or establish there. A claimed preservation
step has the form:

```text
For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').

value.label: Preservation through construction

value.definition: Distinct accounts of construction: algorithmic account states the required operation; informational account states retained meaning and distinctions; computational binding states how work and observations are realised. Cross-account claims identify maps and preservation obligations.

grounding.quote:
The algorithmic account states the required operation, the informational
account the meaning and distinctions retained, and the computational
binding how work and observations are realised
([§2 Accounts of a construction](#accounts-of-a-construction)). A claim
across these accounts identifies its maps and preservation obligations;

claim requires the categorical demonstration above (P1, P6).

conditions: Interpretation is conditional on governing basis and assumptions Γ and declared case domain Ω.

Q_r implies q_t makes q_t necessary; q_t implies Q_r makes it sufficient; a stated conjunction q_1 and ... and q_n implying Q_r makes that conjunction sufficient.

grounding.quote:
For a selected source obligation r, let `Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω)` be its
required predicate over the declared domain Ω of cases. The interpretation
retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted
alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected
text; it does not prove the interpretation faithful (P1, P3).

An assertion targets a predicate `q_t` and states whether that predicate
is the full obligation or a narrower claim. The directions differ:

```text
Q_r implies q_t                   : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
q_t implies Q_r                   : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.

value.definition: A checker has observation map π: Ω → O and admitted evaluation relation T ⊆ O × R, where R is the core algebra. A deterministic checker is functional; human or probabilistic checkers can admit multiple conclusions for identical observations. sat and fal abbreviate judgments about q_t, not execution states.

grounding.quote:
Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and
`T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R is the core result
algebra of Results above. A deterministic checker is a functional special
case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on
the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted
conclusions, not a favourable selected run. `indeterminate` is the core
judgment whose admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate (Results).

value.label: Observation and admitted checker relation

value.definition: Assertion provenance records owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies. Execution provenance records actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment, inputs, observations and result. Assessment authentication separately binds a result to producer, subject, basis and evidence; it establishes neither provenance.

grounding.quote:
An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the
owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared
dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).

value.label: Assertion provenance, execution provenance and authentication

conditions: Compared constructions or assertions are independently justified within their stated scope.
value.definition: Mutual assurance compares constructions or assertions derived along different paths from a common obligation. Requirement-derived assertions check applicable requirement conditions in a realisation; refinement-derived assertions check more detailed obligations. Acceptance and build-level tests are possible examples, not prescribed stages or classes.

grounding.quote:
Construction and assurance can follow different paths from a common
obligation. For `requirement → refinement → realisation`, assertions
derived from the requirement check its applicable conditions in the
realisation; assertions derived from the refinement check its more
detailed obligations there. Acceptance tests and build-level tests can
instantiate these paths
([ASSURANCE §14](ASSURANCE.md#14-design-to-module-evidence-route)); the
roles identify the selected sources and subject in this example and
prescribe no stage names or test classes (P1, P6).

Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or
assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both
being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis

value.label: Parallel derivation and mutual assurance

conditions: Quantitative requirements apply where quantified assurance is claimed.
value.definition: Risk-governed assurance selected by the actor exercising admitted work authority for stated risk, obligations and resource limits. A quantified model describes its population or uncertainty, priors, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. V denotes a specified violation event, E evidence, and M_i a check missing V under specified evaluation conditions.

grounding.quote:
Risk model. The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required
assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That
selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and
uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional
evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and
dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks
substitutes for that account (P6, P5).

Where quantified assurance is claimed, its model states the population or
uncertainty being modelled, prior information, likelihoods, shared causes
and calibration limits. For a specified violation event V and evidence
event E:

value.label: Quantified assurance and risk model

value.definition: Assertion justification explains why a check expresses an obligation; evidence validity identifies dependencies affecting behaviour, conclusion or applicability, including implementation, libraries, data, instruments, environments and assumptions. For change Δ, including a newly invalid assumption, I(Δ) conservatively covers changed facts and affected dependents; D*(t) covers a check's transitive material dependencies in assertion, execution and evidence use; candidate selection S_Δ = {t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ)}.

grounding.quote:
Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct
dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an
obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,
conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,
instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A
requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model (P3, P6).

Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly
discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed
facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover
the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use
of evidence. A candidate selection is:

```text
S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.

value.label: Validity dependencies and impact selection

conditions: Evidence is considered for a new subject and basis.
value.definition: The new evidence account is retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed. Reassessment includes selected checks, new obligations and applicable mandatory gates. Retained evidence keeps its original subject and is used through a new applicability relation; completeness of the combined account differs from freshness of every execution.

grounding.quote:
For a new subject and basis, let `E_old` be the existing evidence records,
`E_reassessed` the evidence newly produced by reassessment, and `E_new`
the resulting account. Reassessment includes the checks selected in
`S_Δ`, the assessment of new obligations and the applicable mandatory
gates. Selection alone produces no execution evidence; failed and
indeterminate results retain their standing:

```text
E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.

value.label: Evidence retention and reassessment

value.definition: The candidate's a_c interpretation and projected views represent material obligations and dependencies under its owning Product's constraint-surface fidelity rule. Five support kinds remain distinct: stated formula, discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked structure, externally assessed predicate, and execution evidence. Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain separate evidence.

grounding.quote:
The candidate's a_c interpretation represents the material obligations
and dependency relationships of these subsections under the
constraint-surface fidelity rule of the Product that owns this corpus,
through [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md) and the acquired
views that project it. It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a
stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked
structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.
An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to
establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.
No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is
selected (P1, P6).

grounding.quote:
Each row records an indexed spelling, the bounded-context identity
declared by the cited owning clause, and the exact owning concept clause.
§17 uses a second row form for a label that several clauses use: the
label, a locator naming where that use occurs, and the owning clause. The
locator only says where to look; it defines nothing and declares no
context, which the owning clause supplies;
§2 states how a row records a concept that a context holds by import, and
a concept whose member declares no bounded context for it.

the occurrence being resolved still supplies its own governed scope (P1,
P3). A row whose context or owning clause does not resolve is invalid, and
this index cannot repair it (P5, P6).

grounding.quote:

predecessor route appears only in §17 as provenance (P6, P3). Each
section names the clause that declares its context. A row's owning concept
clause is the section that defines the concept. Where that section's
member declares the row's context, the clause declares the row's
bounded-context identity and owns the concept, in its own text or through
the context-ownership statement of its own member (P6, P1). Where a
context holds a concept that another member defines, by an import
declaration or by an owner relation that the context's declaring member
states
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members)),
the row cites the defining section as owning concept clause and names the
declaration or owner relation in its relation clause (P1, P3). Otherwise
the relation clause, where given, points to a clause that relates the
concept to another member or context; the index states no relation itself
(P1, P6).

value.definition: F8 identity foundation-to-law table distinguishes consequences from owner-selected policy. Instance premises, not supplied by commitments, are: projects contain many kinds with runtime and domain owners; identities have readable/serialised forms read by people and parsers; projects publish releases whose versions are release coordinates. Row premise sets are: scoped/type/uniqueness P3+(i); stability P3+P4b; boundary claims P3+P6+P5+(i); readable forms P3+P1+(ii); hierarchy P3+(i),(ii); authority split P3+P6+(i); authority conservation P6+P3+P4b; defaults P3+P6; parsing P3+P1+(ii); release boundary P3+P6+(iii); minimum questions P3+P6; implementation policy P3+P1+P0. P0 is recovered, P1/P3/P6 independent, P4b derived from P0/P2, P5 derived from P0/P6 with P0's open-world premise. Choices retain owners: owning authority chooses further coordinates, kinds, readable/opaque/hybrid form and visible serialisation; runtime chooses its generation rules and defaults; domain chooses its grammar, overrides/publication and need for families; issuing authority chooses grants/decisions; profiles choose projection terms; this member chooses the general hierarchy model, grant-field scheme, seven questions and enduring-repair policy. WORLD_MODEL refines the Markov construct, REFERENCE_FRAME owns material sufficiency, FOUNDATIONS owns general authority limits, RELEASE owns release identity.

grounding.quote:
Instance premises,
which the commitments do not supply:

- (i) a governed project holds objects of many kinds, some owned by a
  runtime or engine and some by the domain that defines them;
- (ii) identities are written in serialised or readable forms that people
  and parsers read;
- (iii) a project publishes releases, whose versions are coordinates of
  the release and not of each object.

value.label: F8 premises, consequences and owned choices

value.definition: Object identity is always scoped; its minimum semantic model is authority + kind + value. At minimum it should be interpretable through those coordinates. Additional coordinates may include parent scope, revision, publication version and time.

grounding.quote:
Identity is always scoped. At minimum, identity should be interpretable
through authority, kind and value. So the minimum semantic model is:

```text
identity = authority + kind + value
```

This is the scoped identity of an Object (FOUNDATIONS §2). Optional
additional coordinates may include parent scope, revision, publication
version and temporal coordinates (P3; rc.2 #1-scoped-identity).

value.label: Scoped identity

value.definition: Engine-owned identities concern runtime-owned runs, function calls, jobs, execution frames, continuations and events. Domain-owned identities concern a derived domain's constitutional requirements, requirement families, acceptance criteria, scenarios, ADRs/design decisions and published domain assets. The domain defines its kinds, distinctions, uniqueness and parsing/reading; the runtime may transport these identities.

grounding.quote:
The substrate or runtime may define default identities for runtime-owned
objects, such as runs, function calls, jobs, execution frames,
continuations and events. For these, the engine may use opaque identities and engine-local
generation rules. Those rules should optimise for uniqueness, replay
safety and event-stream integrity. The engine should not impose
domain-specific semantic grammar on domain-owned objects (P3, P6;
rc.2 #engine-owned-identity).

Derived domains own the semantic identity grammar for their own
constitutional objects, such as requirements, requirement families,
acceptance criteria, scenarios, ADRs or design decisions, and published
domain assets. The domain defines which identity kinds exist, how they
are distinguished, what makes them unique, and how they are parsed or
read. The runtime may transport those identities, but it should not
silently invent their meaning (P3, P6; rc.2 #domain-owned-identity).

value.label: Engine-owned and domain-owned identity

value.definition: Authority is an identity-bearing semantic relation preserving owner, kind, governed subject, scope and governing basis; it is not a display label, capability string, actor identity or reachable code path. Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded proxy, whose actor identity remains distinct from human-authority identity.

grounding.quote:
Authority is an identity-bearing semantic relation, not a display label,
capability string, actor identity or reachable code path. Its identity
preserves owner, kind, governed subject, scope and governing basis (P6,
P3; rc.2 #authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004; the Authority
object and its kinds are FOUNDATIONS §2).

value.label: Authority identity

value.definition: Domain override of a bound runtime realisation's identity defaults. Defaults are starter conventions and convenience contracts; their publication and applicable surfaces belong to DESIGN_MODULE §12 realisation law. An override concerns the domain's own identity kinds and is published through domain authority.

grounding.quote:
Default identity formats that a bound runtime realisation publishes are
starter conventions and convenience contracts, not universal doctrine;
they are lawful only so long as derived domains may override them (P3,
P6). What such a realisation publishes, and for which surfaces, is
realisation law outside this member
([DESIGN_MODULE §12](DESIGN_MODULE.md#identity-defaults-from-a-bound-runtime-realisation)).

value.label: Domain identity override

Generalisations replace graph_function/asset_surface/graph_call with published_function/carrier_surface/function_call; graph calls/frames with function calls/execution frames; ABG-specific realisation wording with runtime wording; profile-specific F_H projection with permission for a profile's own term; Id with identity. The defaults-publication permission moves to DESIGN_MODULE §12; identity-law conditions stay here. Release-version selector revision is expressly proposed and pending owner acceptance, while other boundary determinations are claimed unchanged and release forms remain at RELEASE §1.

"Id" is written "identity"; the
predecessor's "must" is written in the indicative and its "should",
"may", "at minimum", "at most", "optional", "useful" and "suitable" keep
their force. Release version boundary: superseded, proposed and pending the product owner's acceptance.
