value.definition: Tier-3 Outcome-Driven Development profile for graph-native product authoring over a declared asset graph. Its graph-native bounded context is urn:stdo:bounded-context:graph-native-odd under the selected complete STDO basis. It owns product shape, graph assets/nodes/vectors/functions/traversals and graph/runtime worker/evaluator shorthands, without absorbing a consuming Product's domain semantics or similarly named concrete runtime carriers. It imports foundation families by reference without restating them. ODD_METHOD rc.2 routes are provenance only.

grounding.quote:
Tier 3. The Outcome-Driven Development profile: graph-native product
authoring over a declared asset graph. It imports the families that
[§1 Foundation to law](#foundation-to-law) lists by reference under
[PROFILES §1](PROFILES.md#1-the-boundary) and restates none of them. Inside
its bounded context it uses its own terms freely: graph, node, asset,
vector, edge, graph function, traversal, worksite, ledger, event log, GTL,
ABG, F_D, F_P and F_H. A route written `rc.2 #anchor` is into
`stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/ODD_METHOD.md` and is provenance
only (P0, P1).

This profile owns those concepts in the graph-native bounded context
`urn:stdo:bounded-context:graph-native-odd` under the selected complete
STDO basis. The context covers the ODD product shape, the GTL language
role, the ABG method role, graph assets, vectors, functions, traversals and
the graph and runtime worker and evaluator shorthands defined here. It does
not absorb a consuming Product's domain semantics, nor a concrete runtime's
carriers that happen to share a spelling (P1, P3).

value.label: ODD profile

value.definition: GTL, Graph Transformation Language, is the typed declarative graph-language capability role and language expression of ODD. ABG is the singular traversal-governance and runtime-truth capability role, realising the GTL program through governance, binding and runtime truth without owning domain-internal HOW. These names denote roles and a construction algebra, not required repositories, packages, vendors or implementations.

grounding.quote:
ODD, GTL and ABG name normative capability roles and a construction
algebra, not a required repository, package, vendor or concrete
implementation. ODD, Outcome-Driven Development, names the graph-native
product-authoring profile. GTL, Graph Transformation Language, names the
role of the typed declarative graph language. ABG names the role of the
singular traversal-governance and runtime-truth authority (P1, P6).

value.label: GTL and ABG capability roles

conditions: A product adopts the ODD profile.
value.definition: F18 foundation-to-law table imports F1 frames/context, F2 transitions/steps/configuration, F3 results/combination, F4 work state/resumption/reuse, F6 claims/evidence/assessment/acceptance, F9 a_c, F10 constitutional chain/outcome/build tenancy, F11 change/ambiguity, F12 project-method binding, F13 work carriers and F15 release/successor conservation; imported rules and choices retain their owners. Adopted instance premises, not foundation-derived, are I1 externally authoritative selected Product outcome; I2 mutable workspace beside immutable ledger/event log; I3 bounded probabilistic constructive workers whose reports/artifacts are observations; I4 building with an installed method-product release, possibly an earlier self-release. P0 is recovered; P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent; P4b derives from P0/P2; P5 derives from P0/P6. The table distinguishes derived consequences from profile and Product choices, lists consumers per row, and attributes rule decisions to their owners rather than consumers.
value.label: F18 imports, instance premises and owned choices

value.definition: The method library distinguishes mutable authoring source for a future cut from installed distributions of one complete selected immutable RC cut. Both contain method members, guides and templates. Method members are constitutional surfaces: predecessor *_METHOD.md files and current README-designated tier-1/tier-2 standards plus tier-3 profiles when selected. *_GUIDE.md guides refine method application as operational guides/application standards. *_TEMPLATE.md templates are reusable starter forms/examples and convenience artifacts only.

grounding.quote:
Both the authoring library and an installed distribution contain three
classes of document. Method members are the constitutional method
surfaces; in the predecessor library they are the `*_METHOD.md` members,
and in this corpus they are the members that [README](README.md#documents)
names as method members: the tier 1 and tier 2 standards and, when a
project selects them, the tier 3 profiles. Guides (`*_GUIDE.md`) are operational guides and application standards
that refine application of the method. Templates (`*_TEMPLATE.md`) are
reusable starter forms and examples and are convenience artifacts only.
Only method members are constitutional method surfaces (P6, P3).

value.label: Method library and document classes

value.definition: An ODD product's declared asset graph expresses state transitions relevant to its work and serves as its declared program/process space.

grounding.quote:
The product is expressed as a declared asset graph over the state
transitions relevant to the product's work (P0, P3).

value.label: Declared asset graph

value.definition: Nodes are durable truth surfaces or product assets, each naming a bounded state of truth. Illustrative software-development names are intent, product, requirements, design, module_decomp, code, uat_testcases, integration_tests, bootloader and build targets; these names are product-local rather than mandatory universal names.

grounding.quote:
Nodes are durable truth surfaces or product assets; each names a bounded
state of truth. In one software-development ODD product the nodes include
`intent`, `product`, `requirements`, `design`, `module_decomp`, `code`,
`uat_testcases`, `integration_tests`, `bootloader` and build targets. Those
names are illustrative and product-local; the law is that nodes name
bounded states (P3).

value.label: ODD node

value.definition: A vector is a lawful/admissible transition between nodes. Each declares required upstream assets, target asset, governing evaluators and gates, and output contract.

grounding.quote:
Vectors are the lawful transitions between nodes and are the admissible
transitions of the product. Each vector declares its required upstream
assets, its target asset, its governing evaluators and gates, and its
output contract (P4a, P6).

value.label: ODD vector

value.definition: Probabilistic compute is bounded constructive work over one declared vector or edge traversal whose worker-internal solution path is not fully determined by graph/runtime. The vector's admissible external space declares upstream assets, target/output contract, context, role/capability expectation, evaluators/gates, provenance obligation and lawful stop/hold/gap/continuation/completion states. ABG may govern, invoke, observe and classify; unconstrained internal HOW includes hidden reasoning, heuristic search, implementation strategy, tool-local execution and product-specific business choice.

grounding.quote:
The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required
upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role
or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance
obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion
states. ABG may govern, invoke, observe and classify the traversal; it
does not own the worker's hidden constructive path. Whatever the traversal
boundary does not constrain remains worker-internal HOW: hidden LLM
reasoning, heuristic search, domain implementation strategy, tool-local
execution detail and product-specific business choice (P0, P6).

value.label: ODD probabilistic compute

value.definition: ODD-local F_P (urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p) is a bounded probabilistic worker turn: bounded non-human construction under declared policy narrowed to one graph traversal contract. ODD-local F_H (urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h) is explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared authority and ambiguity policy, with no ambient traversal, semantic or closure authority. F_D (urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d) is deterministic evaluation/proof over declared traversal properties; it may optimise or validate precise domain-local work without moving domain HOW into GTL, ABG or framework.

grounding.quote:
- `F_P` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`) is the shorthand for the
  bounded probabilistic worker turn. It specialises substrate-neutral
  lawful probabilistic processing: it keeps bounded non-human construction
  under declared policy and narrows that meaning to one graph traversal
  contract.
- `F_D` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-d`) is the shorthand for
  deterministic evaluation or proof over declared properties of the
  traversal. F_D may optimise or validate a domain-local path where the
  domain can make part of the work precise; it does not move domain HOW
  into GTL, ABG or the framework.
- `F_H` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`) is the shorthand for
  explicit human adjudication invoked under the traversal's declared
  authority and ambiguity policy. It specialises the substrate-neutral
  human-adjudication concept and grants a human no ambient traversal,
  semantic or closure authority.

value.label: ODD F_P, F_D and F_H classifications

value.definition: Referenced source concepts for two explicitly declared specialisations: urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing and urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication, with their context owned by SPEC_METHOD §5. Only their preserved meanings stated in ODD are available here; their full owner definitions are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The F_P
specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`; the F_H specialisation runs from
`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication` to
`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-h`. The source concepts and their
context are owned by
[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle); this
profile owns the targets in the graph-native ODD context (P1, P6).

value.label: Referenced probabilistic-processing and human-adjudication sources

value.definition: Graph functions are named constructive programs realising vectors. They may realise an outer vector directly, refine it into a small inner workflow, or act as reusable higher-order library functions. The outer vector remains the constitutional/callable contract. ODD binds ACTIVATION typed refinement to such functions using §11.8's cumulative carried environment as its specialised contract; this remains profile law rather than general core law.

grounding.quote:
Graph functions are named constructive programs that realise vectors. A
graph function may realise one outer vector directly, refine one outer
vector into a small inner workflow, or act as a reusable higher-order
library function. The outer vector remains the constitutional contract;
the graph function is the constructive realisation of that contract (P4a,
P0).

value.label: ODD graph function

value.definition: Source-defined workflow: bind the current target; locate next admissible vectors; traverse one vector; materialise the next asset; prove the vector closed; continue until the selected target closes. This describes a traversal operation without creating or performing a traversal record.

grounding.quote:
The workflow is a traversal over the graph: bind the current target;
locate the next admissible vectors; traverse one vector; materialise the
next asset; prove the vector closed; continue until the selected target
closes. The graph is the declared program space of the product (P0, P5).

value.label: ODD traversal workflow

value.definition: The installed graph-native product provides method, runtime, carrier/control/command surfaces, release-managed methodology and scaffold templates. The distinct target project owns one stdo_<label>.json per distinct Product WHAT, locating constitutional, local/collective reference-frame basis, realisation, work and composition surfaces; its constitutional surfaces; one or more realisation roots bound through how.build_tenants; its domain outputs/evidence. Software examples are GOALS.md, INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md, requirements/, build_tenants/, design/code/tests/documents/proof; these scaffold names are defaults. A clean install is described as installation, authoring target intent/definition/requirements/realisation root, then graph traversal to produce target domain outputs.

grounding.quote:
The graph-native product and the project built with it are distinct. The
installed product provides the method, the runtime and the carrier
surfaces; it does not provide the target project's business domain. The
installed product must not assume prior knowledge of the target project's
domain (P6, P3).

value.label: Installed product and target project

value.definition: A responsibility layer expresses a capability class bound by the product to local domain semantics, with GTL publishing lawful transitions. Illustrative classes are bootstrap/intake, design, implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and retrofit. They are not universal instance names.

grounding.quote:
This profile governs structural responsibility layers and their required
publication shape. It does not freeze one product's local asset names as
universal ODD doctrine. A responsibility layer expresses one capability
class; the product binds that capability to its own local domain
semantics; the GTL carrier publishes the lawful transitions for that bound
capability (P1, P3).

Capability classes may include bootstrap or intake, design,
implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and
retrofit. They are responsibility-layer ideas, not mandatory universal
instance names (P1).

value.label: ODD responsibility layer

value.definition: Audit of a move against the current ODD profile has three outcomes for the predicate 'the move complies with the current profile': compliant maps to satisfied because the move meets current law; non-compliant maps to falsified with the violated law as counterexample; valid and worth incorporating maps to out_of_frame because needed law is undeclared, naming that law, this profile as owner and the required update. Incorporation is neither compliance nor failure.

grounding.quote:
| compliant | satisfied | the move meets the law of the current profile |
| non-compliant | falsified | the law of this profile that the move violates is the counterexample |

value.definition: Any shared contract or carrier materially governing runtime closure, reporting/status truth, topology/frame progression, proof/qualification outcome, event/projection semantics, identity/binding resolution or provider/resolver behaviour. A change capable of altering how multiple surfaces decide current truth is a core-interface change.

grounding.quote: A core interface is any shared contract or carrier that materially governs

value.label: Core interface

value.definition: The explicit migration declaration and inventory, including old-path states remove, replace, re-authorize and temporary scaffolding.

grounding.quote:
Every old path is then classified as `remove`,
`replace`, `re-authorize` or `temporary scaffolding`.

value.label: Required migration protocol

value.definition: Compatibility aliases, fallback identity laws, bridge paths, old readers/writers and proxy or partial interfaces can preserve superseded authority. An explicit live-product compatibility feature is distinguished from current native truth.

grounding.quote:
The only lawful exception is an explicit compatibility
feature retained as part of the live product

value.label: Bridge paths and compatibility features

value.definition: Migration projections, reports, status views and topology views are downstream reflections of authoritative carriers, without a second closure authority.

grounding.quote:
Projections, reports, status views and topology views may reflect the
authoritative carrier; they do not become a second closure surface

value.label: Migration projections

value.definition: Inside-out migration ordering from the new authoritative source carrier to downstream read models, with explicit ticket dependencies and an initially discovered best-guess interface family.

grounding.quote:
Inside-out hard-break migrations proceed from the new authoritative source
carrier outward

value.label: Inside-out first sequencing

value.definition: A migration wave is an ordered set of deliberate hard breaks over one interface family, not a mode licensing ambiguous or competing authority.

grounding.quote: The migration wave is the ordered set of those breaks;

value.label: Hard-break sequence

value.definition: Three distinct proof scopes: per-break rejection/fail-closed proof; bounded intermediate product-slice proof; and complete migration-closure proof after the migration wave.

grounding.quote:
Bounded product-slice
proof may establish only the exact intermediate outcome permitted by the
path-relative promotion rule

value.label: Migration proof scopes

value.definition: Completion across the declared affected migration scope, distinct from accepted intermediate slices. Retention is a justification relation for a superseded mechanism serving a distinct currently supported responsibility.

grounding.quote: Retention bears the burden.

value.label: Migration closure and retention

value.definition: A constitutional reset on a new branch, version line or methodology basis. Prior constitutional documents become source material; prior design/code may be references. Constitutional adoption states are adopted, superseded, deferred and orphaned. Implementation states are carry_across (materially same, explicitly re-adopted), redundant (unneeded), and rewrite (needed but rebuilt under new requirements/design). These adoption states differ from live requirement standing and from RELEASE §9 predecessor-claim dispositions.

grounding.quote: fundamental migration is controlled adoption, not passive preservation.

value.label: Fundamental migration and adoption states

value.definition: Refactor and migration are described as a transformation wave over mutable implementation surfaces, with restricted temporary mixed state while in flight and one current operative surface across the affected scope when landed.

grounding.quote:
Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over
mutable
implementation surfaces

value.label: Transformation wave

value.definition: Source-defined application of ACTIVATION's step to agentic/probabilistic construction: accepted basis, bounded affected relations, selected computational relations, delegated execution/decision authority, construction/self-review, independent live-surface assessment where required, owner disposition, accepted checkpoint and next already-authorised action. Candidate availability, assessment and accept/local_repair/re_enter/reject disposition are separate results. Preservation, progress and completion are separate construction claims. Tenant binding supplies execution means and resource limits; configuration selects frames and return consumer.

grounding.quote:
a candidate that is available or
assessed is not thereby accepted

value.label: Bounded execution

value.definition: Evidence for constitutional realisation claims: authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible, and present-tense residual open pressure. Proof identity/adequacy, semantic/evidence/projection separation and assurance congruence/qualification belong to EVALUATION; verification layers, testing taxonomy, fixture/proof portability, test authority, scenario bundles, installed proof and significant-path coverage belong to ASSURANCE.

grounding.quote:
includes an authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof
where drift is plausible, and a present-tense statement of the residual
open pressure

value.label: Realisation evidence

value.definition: An ADR records a design decision boundary: the choice making acceptance criteria true. Its fields are Status (active/superseded/retired), Implements requirement identifiers, Derives from intent identifier or strategy, Supersedes prior ADR/doctrine, Superseded by successor when superseded, and Retained special case when earlier behaviour is intentionally retained. ADR files are constitutional sources; an optional REGISTRY.md is a potentially drifting read model.

grounding.quote: ADRs are written per decision boundary, not per requirement file;

value.label: Architectural decision record

value.definition: One independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a product's WHAT, located by its product-definition tenant registry. One WHAT has one or more independent tenants regardless of layout. A tenant owns its binding, realisation and evidence; tenant-local truth remains derivative until ratified in specification.

grounding.quote:
A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a
  product's WHAT.

value.label: Build tenant

value.definition: The product WHAT's obligations, permitted outcomes and rules for refining and composing realisation work.

grounding.quote:
The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its
  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and
  composing the work that realises it.

value.label: Requirements calculus

value.definition: A declared set of executable operations, composition laws, permitted transformations, effects and resource behaviour insofar as material to obligations.

grounding.quote: A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,

value.label: Computational calculus

value.definition: Concrete means performing operations: technology stack, human process of people/roles/documents/channels/decision procedures, or both. Author identity, actor identity and operation kind are distinct; operation kind combines what it does, such as construct/assess/relay/record/measure/decide, with required authority. A generic procedure has scope independent of the chosen environment.

grounding.quote:
An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those
  operations:

value.label: Execution environment and operation kinds

value.definition: Two-part tenant design relation: calculus binding from requirements calculus to computational calculus, and execution binding from computational calculus to concrete environment. The registry locates a tenant but is not its binding. Algorithmic, informational and computational accounts remain distinct across the binding.

grounding.quote: A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts:

value.label: Build-tenant binding

value.definition: The subject's provenance ledger for predecessor rc.2 rows received locally or routed to tier-1/other members. Conserved rows are asserted to be restated at their receiving loci; routes are provenance only. It records generalisation of graph-specific wording, filenames, prefixes, overlay fields and profile shorthand; retained profile scope and modal force; proposed supersessions pending product-owner acceptance; newly authored distinctions; and receiving owners. Its entries are subject claims, not this interpretation's acceptance or fidelity findings.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is
restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is provenance only.

value.label: Source disposition ledger

value.definition: Tier-2 T-area standard owning the unified work-carrier model, layout/bindings, sprint/ticket rules, triage metadata and upward propagation, carrier selection and carrier-side execution admission, execution/verification separation, J/O continuity, closure/reuse, test-case authority, migration-ticket mechanics, one-truth projection, recommended shapes and operating mode. It realises FOUNDATIONS, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION rather than supplying foundational law; mechanisms may differ under the same principles.

grounding.quote: Tier 2. Owns the work carriers of the method:

value.label: TICKETS standard

value.definition: The current epic layer located by ticketing.goals, with GOALS.md the default file. Goals state active work wave and present priorities, broader than a ticket but narrower and more current than intent; they are not durable execution-tracking units.

grounding.quote:
Goals are
broader than one ticket, narrower and more current than the intent surface,

value.label: Ticketing goals

value.definition: One typed durable source-of-truth record per work unit, enduring across sessions; one Markdown file is the default carrier. Tickets are used where feature work, bugs, spikes or chores need independent durable identity, with bugs and features sharing one system.

grounding.quote: Tickets are the enduring work records. Each ticket is one durable record,

value.label: Ticket record

value.definition: TICKETS' bounded execution batch: one manifest under optional ticketing.sprints.root, default .ai-workspace/sprints/, batching authority references, closure law, evidence expectations and local deferred compliance. It closes through explicit sprint-close review, may contain durable tickets, manifest-local iterations or both, and holds batch authority without constitutional authority.

grounding.quote: Sprints are bounded execution batches.

value.label: Ticketing sprint

value.definition: A POSTING_GUIDE post on the board bound by ticketing.comments.root, default .ai-workspace/comments/, publishing ideas, strategy, reviews, handoffs, closure summaries and reasoned decisions. It has no task-status authority and no independent decision authority; a recorded decision obtains authority only by adoption on its owning surface.

grounding.quote: Comments are not task status authority.

value.label: Comment

value.definition: A run-scoped admitted work surface derived from a ticket, a sprint manifest plus included ticket/iteration, or intake drafting when no durable or sprint-local identity is needed. Unlike a ticket surviving sessions/work waves or a sprint surviving its batch and close review, it is the admitted execution function for one run; it is neither a rival backlog nor a second planning surface.

grounding.quote:
An execution contract is the run-scoped
admitted work surface

value.label: Execution contract

value.definition: A closure-bearing bounded work claim within a ticket, with stable identity, dependencies, current state, required evidence and explicit relation to ticket closure. Multiple milestones do not make multiple tickets.

grounding.quote:
A ticket may contain several closure-bearing milestones without becoming
several tickets.

value.label: Milestone and phase-scoped claim

value.definition: Starter layout: stdo_default.json; specification/GOALS.md; .ai-workspace/sprints/; .ai-workspace/tickets/{backlog,active,completed}/; and .ai-workspace/comments/<agent-id>/. This is a default carrier layout rather than a required physical structure.

grounding.quote: The starter file layout

value.label: Default ticketing layout

value.definition: Product-definition bindings locate epic goals (ticketing.goals), optional sprint batches/close review (ticketing.sprints.root), authoritative ticket lanes (ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog, .active, .completed), and discussion/publication (ticketing.comments.root). The definition locates carriers without owning their ticket/comment content. A generated board is ordinarily a projection.

grounding.quote:
The definition locates these carriers and
does not own their ticket or comment content.

value.label: Ticketing bindings and board projections

value.definition: Substitution or extension of the valid default durable-local-file model by other bound carriers, generated boards, dependency checks, links to scenario/requirement/ADR surfaces, external tracker sync or standard-tool-protocol message integration, preserving authority and refusal laws.

grounding.quote: Another carrier is not required to reproduce its folders,

value.label: Carrier substitution

value.definition: One durable manifest record per sprint, defaulting to a Markdown file; another bound carrier retains its identity, required fields, history, closure law and one-truth relation. A stable id and short filename slug are recommended; SPRINT-2026-04-30-process-navigator.md and SPRINT-2026-05-12-dashboard-density.md are naming examples.

grounding.quote: Each sprint has one durable manifest record;

value.label: Durable sprint manifest

value.definition: Minimum sprint states: active admits iteration inside the boundary; closing freezes new iteration while close review/paydown classification run; closed means review finished and remaining debt accepted, ticketed, repriced or removed; superseded means an unsuitable boundary was replaced by a new authority surface, sprint or ticket set. Planned and cancelled are optional additions.

grounding.quote:
The minimum sprint status model is `active`, `closing`, `closed` and
`superseded`

value.label: Sprint status domain

value.definition: Batch-level admission under a reviewable manifest boundary, distinct from the universal intake and constitutional authority governing included work.

grounding.quote:
A sprint may admit work only when the manifest makes the boundary
reviewable.

value.label: Sprint admission

value.definition: Explicit sprint-held deferral of local compliance proof or cleanup, conditioned on local reviewable debt and favourable correction-versus-per-change-proof cost, with close-review classification and paydown. Escrow is not acceptance or silent debt.

grounding.quote:
Deferred compliance is not
silent debt: it is escrow held by the sprint,

value.label: Compliance escrow

value.definition: Review of each included sprint item under the authority cited by its manifest. Its six outcomes are accepted, local_paydown, design_reframe, requirement_reprice, product_reprice and remove. For the predicate 'the reviewed item is accepted as compliant under the sprint authority', their mappings are respectively accept/satisfied, local_repair/falsified, re_enter/invalid_basis, re_enter/invalid_basis, re_enter/invalid_basis and no matching disposition/falsified. Local debt supplies the local_paydown counterexample while the governing relation remains coherent; a necessary authority change instead requires repricing. Removal supplies a counterexample without requiring a violated governing relation or competing truth path. Repricing names the re-entry layer as a declared domain fact accompanying the core value. Debt-entry outcomes accepted, ticketed, repriced and removed map respectively to accept/satisfied, local_repair/falsified, re_enter/invalid_basis and no disposition/falsified, for the separate predicate 'the debt entry is accepted under the sprint authority'.

grounding.quote: | `remove` | none | falsified | the work is backed out or kept out of closure; the reason for removal is the counterexample. No disposition of ACTIVATION §3 has this condition, because removal does not require a violated governing relation or a competing truth path |

sprint authority": accepted matches `accept` (`satisfied`), ticketed
matches `local_repair` (`falsified`), removed takes `falsified` with no
matching disposition, and repriced matches `re_enter`
(`invalid_basis`), on the grounds of `accepted`, `local_paydown`,

value.label: Sprint close review and result mappings

value.definition: A durable unit of work with one authoritative record. One markdown file is the default carrier; repository or external-tracker carriers are conditional alternatives.

grounding.quote:
Each ticket has one durable authoritative record; the default carrier is
one markdown file.

value.label: Ticket

value.definition: One admitted upstream work item with more than one build-tenant execution line, within urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy. The upstream authority and each tenant-local ticket have distinct identities and lifecycles. The three lawful cases are upstream-only authority with no tenant duplicate yet; a single tenant-local execution line without required siblings; and one upstream authority ticket plus one suffixed tenant-local ticket per execution line.

grounding.quote:
A multi-build-tenant work item is one admitted upstream work item with more
than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each
tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles.

value.label: Multi-build-tenant work

value.definition: The kind of work record. The minimum common set is feature, bug, spike and chore; the default set is expected to suffice for most cases.

grounding.quote:
The minimum common set of ticket types is `feature`, `bug`, `spike` and
`chore`. A project may add more; the default set should be enough for
most cases

value.label: Ticket type

value.definition: The execution or migration discipline governing a ticket, orthogonal to type. Its minimum common set is ordinary and implementation_migration; feature, bug, spike and chore can each carry either category.

grounding.quote:
Ticket category is orthogonal to ticket type: type answers what kind of
work record this is; category answers what execution or migration
discipline governs the ticket (P3, P1; rc.2 #ticket-category). The minimum
common set is `ordinary` and `implementation_migration`, so a `feature`,
`bug`, `spike` or `chore` may carry either.

value.label: Ticket category

conditions: ticket_category is implementation_migration
value.definition: A governed replacement of one implementation truth path by another across producers, consumers, projections and proof surfaces. Examples include replacing a tracker or read-model family with one authoritative carrier, introducing a public interface requiring migration of every producer and consumer before closure, and removing a bridge or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.

grounding.quote:
`implementation_migration` is
used when the ticket is not "change code until tests pass" but a governed
replacement of one implementation truth path with another across producers,
consumers, projections and proof surfaces: a bug ticket that replaces an old
tracker or read-model family with one new authoritative carrier; a feature
ticket that introduces a new public interface and requires every producer
and consumer to migrate before closure; a refactor ticket that removes a
bridge path or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.

value.label: Implementation migration ticket

value.definition: The intake-triage declaration of where a change lawfully re-enters the constitutional chain, using SPEC_METHOD §4 classes. Common, nonexclusive pairings are feature with goal_reprice, intent_reprice, product_reprice, requirement_reprice or design_reframe; bug with requirement_reprice, design_reframe or realization_refactor; and chore with design_reframe or realization_refactor. A spike is exploratory but still carries its current triage class.

grounding.quote:
Ticket type and change class are orthogonal: type answers what kind of
work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully
re-enters the constitutional chain. A ticket records the `change_class`
declared by intake triage, using the classes of
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) (P4b, P2; rc.2
#change-class).

value.label: Change class

value.definition: Ticket statuses have the minimum domain backlog, active and completed. Lanes locate those states: backlog is accepted durable work outside current execution focus; active is the current bounded execution set; completed is closed work retained as history. Ticket and local statuses, lanes, sprint statuses, migration_strategy, library_usage and recorded change_class are declared carrier states, not evaluation results.

grounding.quote:
The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the
sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`
values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map
to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under
[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes).

`backlog`
is accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part of the
current execution focus; `active` is the current bounded execution set;
`completed` is closed work retained as history.

value.label: Ticket states and lanes

value.definition: One run-scoped contract for each execution governed by the source method, derived from the smallest lawful carrier for the required lifetime after establishing upstream work authority. Its minimum state domain includes drafted, admitted, rejected and superseded. A ticket-shaped contract describes categorisation, closure criteria, proof surface, non-closure conditions and required contract fields; that shape creates neither durable ticket identity nor ticket-lane state.

grounding.quote:
Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution
contract. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the
smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream
work authority, then select the first matching row below. For work inside
an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it
is the current run

the contract carries at minimum the states named in ACTIVATION §1
(drafted, admitted, rejected, superseded).

value.label: Run-scoped execution contract

value.definition: F13 is the source's work-carrier family: selection of the record carrying work, its permitted claims and closure. Instance premises concern lifetimes, several apparent state surfaces, several build tenants, truth-path migrations and variation among files, trackers and services. The table distinguishes consequences, local domain or policy choices, their owners and consumer loci. Cited standing is P0 recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and P2 with the non-reacquirable step-fact premise; and P5 derived from P0 and P6 with the open-world premise. Local choices include carrier kinds and selection, sprint availability and mechanics, fields/types/categories/statuses/lanes/shapes, tenant suffixes, migration declarations and review conventions, repricing states and reconciliation order. Product definition owns carrier bindings, admission mechanism, evidence surface and tenant identity; the governing method owns whether sprint debt can survive.

grounding.quote:
This family (F13 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law))
decides which record carries a piece of work, what that record may claim
and when the work closes. Its instance premises, which the commitments do
not supply, are named in the rows as follows: lifetimes, work and its
obligations last one run, one bounded batch or longer; several surfaces,
goals, tickets, comments, boards and summaries can each appear to state
the same work state; several tenants, one work item may be realised in
more than one build tenant; migrations, some work replaces one
authoritative truth path with another across producers, consumers and
proofs; carriers vary, a project may keep its carriers in files, trackers
or services. Each commitment's standing is written as the table of
commitments in FOUNDATIONS §3 states it.

value.label: F13 work-carrier family

value.definition: Ticket and work-instruction terms whose meanings resolve through PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5 bounded-context semantic resolution, using the cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis and affected scope.

grounding.quote:
Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under the bounded-context
semantic resolution of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5. A ticket may use an
unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis
and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning (P1, P3;
rc.2 #bounded-context-term-binding).

value.label: Bounded-context term binding

value.definition: Migration declaration state with values inside_out_hard_break and fundamental_re_adoption. The former orders breaks from deepest source truth outward; the latter records explicit human product-authority selection and adjudication of inherited implementation as carry_across, redundant or rewrite.

grounding.quote:
The required fields are `migration_strategy`, with the values
`inside_out_hard_break` and `fundamental_re_adoption`, and
`library_usage`, with the values `none`, `consume` and `extend`.

value.label: Migration strategy

value.definition: Migration declaration state none, consume or extend, recording whether the active boundary rebuilds locally, consumes an existing reusable library/commonisation surface, or extends it before the local implementation lands.

grounding.quote:
An implementation migration ticket declares whether the active boundary is
rebuilding a pattern locally, consuming an existing reusable library or
commonisation surface, or extending that surface before the local
implementation lands; `library_usage` records which (P2, P4a; rc.2
#recurring-realization-and-library-declaration).

value.label: Library usage declaration

value.definition: Assessment distinct from construction output and from the decision owner's acceptance disposition. The reviewer is not the reviewed subject's author. Tier-1 protocol, acceptance and reuse are referenced to EVALUATION §§3,5 and ACTIVATION §7; this member supplies work-carrier requirements and its independent-review boundary policy.

grounding.quote:
The generic law is tier 1: a constructor's self-review is construction
output and the independent-assessment protocol is
[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment); acceptance as the
decision owner's disposition, and closure by stated condition rather than
by reviewer approval, is [EVALUATION §5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance); reuse
of a closed result is [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).
This section states what those laws require of work carriers.

value.label: Independent assessment

value.definition: Distinct reusable records of residual judgment J and owner ruling O, supported by computed facts C as applicable. J records a question, exact subject/basis, facts/evidence, actor/authority, conclusion/scope, uncertainty and concrete revising observation. O records original wording, owner, exact subject/basis, permitted scope/effects, conditions and source separately from agent interpretation. Repricing dispositions retained, superseded, deferred and withdrawn are owner-set obligation states, not core results, candidate acceptance or predecessor-claim qualification.

grounding.quote:
A residual judgment that another activation needs is recorded once, with
its owning work, in the existing carrier selected under §5. The record
identifies the question; the exact subject and governing basis; the
supporting computed facts and evidence; the responsible actor and its
authority; the conclusion and its scope; the uncertainty; and a concrete
revising observation that lets a consumer determine whether the conclusion
still applies.

value.label: Recorded judgment and owner ruling

value.definition: A bounded work claim whose completion is evaluated over every applicable declared obligation, exact subject/basis/scope, applicable judgments and rulings, and active non-closure conditions. The source identifies this condition with FOUNDATIONS §4 conjunction of results and makes this section its owner; SPEC_METHOD's consistency gate applies it over a change span.

grounding.quote:
A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope; every
required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
reserved acceptance

value.label: Work claim and condition-based closure

value.definition: A proof projection from admitted work authority. The recommended substantive-test derivation is ticket → intake triage → lawful re-entry point → governing requirement, design, module, published function, carrier or closure surface → test expectation. Implementation behavior is evidence, not the authority determining the expected result.

grounding.quote:
ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
design, module, published function, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation

value.label: Test case authority

value.definition: One work-state authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, tickets own ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone state, and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections. Surface questions remain distinct: goals identify the current broad wave; SPEC_METHOD identifies constitutional class/re-entry; sprints identify a bounded proof/evidence/paydown batch; tickets identify durable work and state; comments record proposals, arguments, decisions, reviews and handoffs; POSTING_GUIDE specifies comment publication structure and naming.

grounding.quote:
Work state has one authority chain: goals own the bounded work wave, the
ticket owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone
state (§1), and accepted design owns realisation decisions. Comments,
dashboards, registers, indexes and generated summaries are projections
(P6, P3; rc.2 #one-truth-state-projection-and-drift-refusal-stdo-up-009).

The goals surface: what broad work wave
matters now. SPEC_METHOD: what constitutional change class and re-entry
point govern the work. Sprints: what bounded execution batch is currently
pricing proof, evidence and paydown. Tickets: what durable units of work
exist and what state they are in. Comments: what was proposed, argued,
decided, reviewed or handed off. POSTING_GUIDE: how comment-layer
publications are structured and named.

value.label: Work-state authority and projections

value.definition: Three recommended document shapes, presented as examples rather than instantiated work. The sprint example SPRINT-2026-04-30-operational-projection is active under goal operational-projection-ux, with opened/updated timestamps 2026-04-30T09:00:00Z, references to GOALS, PRODUCT and a governing design surface, and scope limited to layout/readability/interaction/visual evidence. It excludes product truth, data contract, runtime/governance semantics and new constructive carriers; expects realization_refactor; includes UXI-001 relation-line readability work, screenshot evidence and pending contrast debt; and illustrates timebox/surface-volume/design-lead close triggers, forensic walkthrough, screenshots/notes, deferred screenshots/accessibility/replay review, hidden-drift non-closure and paydown/repricing. The ordinary example T-001, Add Product Layer To SPEC_METHOD, is an active feature/ordinary ticket for methodology-bootstrap with product_reprice, product re-entry, high priority and triage/creation/update date 2026-04-07. Its acceptance concerns PRODUCT.md in the chain, intent → product → requirements bootstrap, and aligned examples/reconstruction, with a comment link. The migration example B-010 is an active bug/implementation_migration ticket using inside_out_hard_break and library_usage none because the boundary-specific pattern is not recurring; goal operator-gap-truth, design_reframe, design_surface re-entry and date 2026-04-20. It replaces fallback gap projection with synthetic convergence fields by declared-obligation projection plus separately classified fallback gaps, within the operator-query acceptance path and with no excluded scopes. It identifies old/new producers, shared query/summary/review consumers, gap/span/negative-proof derived surfaces, the removal-of-old-authority closure law, and an unchecked migration checklist.

grounding.quote:
These shapes are the recommended carriers of the fields and sections the
rules above require; a project may bind another shape that carries the
same fields (§2; P3, P4b; rc.2 #recommended-ticket-shape).
- closure_law: migration closes only when the old projection is no longer authoritative within the affected scope and mixed old/new proof does not count as acceptance

value.label: Recommended sprint and ticket templates

value.definition: The source's provenance ledger for received rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md rows, distinguishing conserved rows, heading-only non-applicability, loci and new statements. Routes are provenance only and conserved rows are claimed to be restated locally. Reported generalisations replace graph/AssetSurface and UX terminology with published-function/public-carrier and user-interface terminology; F_D-like/F_P-like phrases with deterministic/constructive-or-probabilistic phrases; Executive appointment with coordinating appointment; design-method law with design-profile law; and the old work-carrier context reference with PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8. Section 6 and 8 code blocks are claimed verbatim, including American spellings and Product. The family table, declared-state/result distinctions for carrier states and obligation repricing states, and sprint result mappings are described as new; the table decides no more than cited rules.

grounding.quote:
Rows of rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md received by this member. Anchors are into
rc.2 TICKET_METHOD.md; a locus is a section of this file unless another
member is named. Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

value.label: Source provenance and disposition ledger

conditions: Adoption is optional and is not implied by availability.
value.definition: Tier-3, application-neutral model-family signature for immutable traversal-application histories over an externally changing subject.
